claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I have one child I'd like to check eligibility for. His name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I have one child to assess - Alex.

Before I can determine eligibility, I need to gather some details. Let me start with:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to understand Alex's current situation better.

**Is Alex in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's still in sixth form doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Now I need to understand your living situation.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good. Now I need to check a few more important details about Alex's circumstances.

**Is Alex in any form of care, hospital, or custody arrangement - for example, in foster care, a children's home, young offenders' institution, or hospital?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He just lives here with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I just need to clarify one more thing about your situation.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?** (This relates to residency requirements for Child Benefit eligibility.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me just clarify one final detail to complete my assessment.

**Do you have any other children besides Alex that you'd like me to check eligibility for?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility. Let me read the official guidance to ensure I apply the rules correctly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on the official guidance I've reviewed, I can now provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Even though Alex is 18, you can still receive Child Benefit for him because he's in full-time approved education (A-levels in sixth form). The rules allow Child Benefit to continue for young people up to age 20 if they remain in approved education or training.

All the key criteria are met:
- Alex lives with you
- He is in full-time approved education
- He's not in hospital, care, or any custody arrangement
- You are a UK resident

You should be able to make a claim for Child Benefit now. If you need help with the application process, you can contact HMRC directly.
